items.note: The page carries out the whole signed Kronecker substitution as the paper does: evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, the four products of absolute values, centered-residue extraction justified by |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<2^{3p}<B_0/2, the reduction modulo y^r+1, truncation, and the cost. It spells out the separation argument that the assignment asks for.

From 'coefficients are 2^{-p} times Gaussian integers of modulus at most 2^p' the page writes f=2^{-p}(a+ib), g=2^{-p}(c+ie) with integer coefficients of absolute value at most 2^p and sets B_0=2^{4p}, matching the paper. The hypothesis that r is a power of two (r>=2) comes through R_r, and the page states r<2^p.

'By the geometric sum, |A_u|<=2^p(B_0^r-1)/(B_0-1)<B_0^r/2, so its magnitude fits in 4pr bits' gives the paper's bound and its consequence. Like the paper, it leaves the second inequality (2^{p+1}<B_0-1) implicit.

The page explains that the multiplier needs nonnegative inputs, multiplies the absolute values, restores signs, pads h_{2r-1}=0, and writes A_aA_c=(ac)(B_0)=sum h_jB_0^j, as the paper does. Its sign rule is slightly imprecise when an operand is zero (see errors).

'Each h_j sums at most r products of coefficients of size at most 2^p, so |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<2^{3p}<B_0/2' uses the stated r<2^p for the middle inequality. The uniqueness of the centered residue is then proved in the extraction paragraph.

The page reproduces the carry recurrence, the bound -B_0<u_j+gamma_j<B_0 that keeps gamma_j in {-1,0}, and the telescoped identity. It then goes beyond the paper and checks both sign cases and why complement-and-increment yields B_0^r-(A_u+B_0^r)=|A_u|.

The extraction carry is defined as in the paper and shown to lie in {0,1} 'since q_j+rho_j in [0,B_0]'. Equality hat h_j=h_j follows by induction through the prefix identity sum_{i<j}q_iB_0^i=sum_{i<j}h_iB_0^i+rho_jB_0^j, which is equivalent to the paper's residual identity. The separation bound, including the padded zero, finishes the argument.

The page gives the streams ac-be and ae+bc and justifies the wrap 'Since y^{j+r}=-y^j' by subtracting the coefficient at j+r from the one at j. The missing top coefficient is covered by the earlier padding h_{2r-1}=0.

The page uses the paper's counting argument (exactly one j_2 for each j_1, with the sign set by whether j_1+j_2=j or j+r) to get |H_j|<=r2^{2p}. It then deduces that each coefficient 2^{-2p}H_j/r of fg/r has modulus at most 1, so fg/r lies in the disk.

items.note: Truncation is a shift by p+log_2 r bits, giving error below sqrt2*2^{-p}. Each 4pr-bit product costs O(rp log(rp)) and every other stage is a constant number of linear scans, so the four products dominate, as in the paper. The page never says that the truncated output stays in the disk.

errors.quote: A product is negative when exactly one operand is.
errors.problem: This is false when the other operand is zero: the product is then 0 and must not get a negative sign. Complementing and incrementing a 'negative' zero within a fixed width would give the wrong sign extension. The correct rule is that the product is negative when exactly one operand is negative and neither is zero. The paper says only 'restore each product's sign'.
